text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's banking climate is still very good, a recent survey of the banking community by Rzeczpospolita said.
The results do not confirm the conclusions of previous polls by the Pentor polling institute and the Polish Banking Association, which forecasted a decline in credit action.
- The Augustow-based PWT Augustow cigarette maker will change its name to British American Tobacco Polska SA as of January 1, 1996, BAT Group Poland president Louis Hughes said.
The company will make and sell the Jan III Sobieski, Lucky Strike, HB and Nord cigarette brands.
- The Krakow-based Oknoplast window maker will soon start a new production line which will increase its monthly output to 8,000 windows made on license from Germany's Veka AG.
- Poland's drug makers plan to consolidate their production facilities and marketing operations, the plants' board directors said at a symposium organised by Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy SA.
- The Gdynia shipyard's management has complained that the envisaged consolidation in a shipbuilding holding recently proposed by the Szczecin shipyard is not fair for the Gdynia-based plant.
- Trade turnover between Poland and Germany's eastern lands has exceeded the turnover betweeen Poland and the former East Germany before 1989.
A further 30-percent increase is expected next year.
NOWA EUROPA
- The number of wood processing plants in Trzebownisko, eastern Poland, grew from 20 to 178 in the last three years due to a soaring increase in Russian and Ukrainian furniture imports.
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA, Poland's telecom monopolist, will in the next two years invest 20 million zlotys in the construction of a transmission mast in Kalisz province, western Poland.
- Poland's Cadena Data auditing software maker has received full membership in the international Exact Software Group, which unites the industry's quality makers.
- Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) recommended holding Okocim brewery shares in its November report.
- Polish and Moroccan firms will start forming seafood prcocessing joint ventures as of January 1997 in accordance with agreements between the two countries signed last week.
- The Gant money exchange chain, which operates in southwestern Poland, has sent a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commiossion (KPW), Gant president Grzegorz Antkowiak said.
- Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy will be an adviser in the privatisation of the country's biggest electric power distributor, GZE in southern Poland, the company's fianancial director Halina Bukowa said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The 1996 losses of the Warsaw-based Ursus tractor maker losses will reach 35 million zlotys, company general director Janusz Sciskalski said.
- The recently formed Fischer Centrum, a subsidiary of the listed Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum automotive group, will start producing, assembling and marketing bicycles in January next year, Zasada said.
- Poland's second biggest insurance firm, Warta SA, will publish the new prices of its obligatory transport insurance policies, Warta said.
- In the first nine months of this year 16 companies belonging to National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 2 made net profits, while 23 firms made losses, NFI 2 said.
